items.title: 69537_Jimmy Jones oral history interview
items.q: I would like to speak about who I think is a great singer and a great friend of mine, Joe Williams. We were kids, in our early teens, I suppose, and we used to play on softball teams and baseball teams, neighborhood competition, in our early days.

ctx.x: No, we didn't have any arrangements. I didn't start writing -- I started writing, after I left her, writing for her after I left her, when I began to free lance in New York, and I started writing for Joe Williams, Sarah, and Lena, and you know, there was a bunch of them. And I was just the accompanist at that time.
But you did beautiful things with her, behind her. It was a very effective combination, you and Sarah.

items.title: Joe Williams interviewed by Leslie Gourse, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...Jimmy Jones and everyone. [INTERVIEWEE] Yup, yup, yup, yup, yup. Hank Jones, Jimmy Jones, Osie Johnson...

ctx.x: Harry “Sweets” Edison, and I like that Bohanon, the trombonist you worked with, and so many of them. I mean I love them. Jimmy Jones and everyone.
Yup, yup, yup, yup, yup. Hank Jones, Jimmy Jones, Osie Johnson, Milt Hinton, Kenny Burrell, oh boy, Romeo Penque, Harold Lookofsky. Really all these wonderful — Zoot Sims, Frank Foster, and —
And the Jones-Lewis band. The Thad Jones-Mel Lewis band.
